sections.title: The Material Landscapes of Mediterranean Islands, scientific approaches
sections.description:
Embark on a journey through the rich histories and material identities of Mediterranean islands in the ancient past. In this introductory course, we will explore key themes of Mediterranean archaeology focusing on natural resources, landscape, and island connectivity. From the Penn Museum’s archaeological collections to foundational methods in science and technology in archaeology, we will approach ancient landscapes of agriculture and pastoralism, the mining of rocks, salt and metal, and the emergence of island cultures up to 1000 CE. Students will delve
into the internal and external forces that drove regional exchange of goods and power, influenced ancient land and resource management, and shaped ancient lifeways. Course lessons will be reinforced by a week-long trip across Sicily, which will serve as this year’s island case study. On this excursion, students will directly experience the ‘Connected Mediterranean’ as they visit archaeological sites and collections, traverse the landscapes, taste local cuisine, and stand inside settlements influenced by successive regional powers such as the Sicels, Phoenicians, Greeks and Arabs.
